I'm not sure why they call this a gift set, because they arrive in a plain brown package that does not look very exciting, and then when you pull out the cool paints, most of them have fallen out of their trays because there are no lids and the trays are so flexible that they just move and the paints just slide right out. Why didn't they put this in a firm plastic case with a lid of some kind? Unfortunately, I am taking an old Crayola paint container that I had and having to pop out the paint from these cheap little trashy plastic trays and put them into my old Crayola paint container. This is certainly not something that should be considered a gift set, and certainly does not feel deluxe in any way. I do like the paper that they gave us that is basically like watercolor paper only with some coloring outlines there, so it's basically a watercolor coloring book. It's sort of a miniature size that is really cute and fun for small projects. If they were just to address the format and packaging here, this would be a real win. As it is, it is hard to recommend something that is not in a firm enough plastic tray to actually make use by children easy.

AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players Ok hear me out for a minute before I explain why I didn't give it a better rating. My wife and I love The Office. We consider ourselves huge fans-- buuut maybe not quite to the point of super fans because we can be forgetful on certain things about the show occasionally. But we are those people that, if you tell us a story, we'll likely have an Office reference to match it. So we were excited about getting to try this out.

This is where I might be a little too picky about it…well, I'm just going to say a little passionate about it lol. But if it's a classic game with a different theme (such as this one)-- it's usually directed toward people who are big fans of that specific theme...that likely will be expecting certain details. Otherwise, if they aren't fans, or real into that theme, they will probably just get the classic/original version...or go for a different theme that they are fans of. So if you're leaving big parts out, you're likely going to have some disappointed fans.

I also realize that there's so much great things about the show and so I'm sure it's hard to narrow it all down to a select amount of cards. So I give some credit to that.

My reasons for rating it lower:

Nearly all of the cards are of Michael, Dwight, Jim and Pam. Then there's randomly one of Kelly and the special rule/twist card with Kevin....but no one else is part of the game?! And yes, the ones included are amazing actors/characters and all...but many of the other regulars are, too- and all together they made The Office.

There are cards for numbers 0-9 (they each have the different colors) and 6 action cards. So that's 16 different pictures they could utilize. Which means there are enough to feature the regular characters…I'll list/count out the ones that come to my mind 1-Michael, 2-Dwight, 3-Jim, 4-Pam, 5-Angela, 6.Kevin, 7-Oscar, 8-Creed, 9-Meredith, 10-Stanley, 11-Phyllis, 12-Kelly, 13-Ryan, 14-Toby, 15-Darryl.

I also felt like some of the photos could have been better selected. I won't rant on too much about that, and spare you, but a quick example-- Kevin's chili twist card isn't of that actual scene just him at his desk. And why not put Toby as the draw 4 card, instead 😄

I do like the picture of the back-side of the cards, the wild card with Michael dancing in the Diwali episode and *some* of the other pics they chose.

The card and photo quality is really good. My box container was torn a little at the top.

It is still fun to play, I do like the special rule/twist for Kevin's chili, and like the idea of The Office theme but I do think it could be improved upon by including more characters.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players

Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple I got the Easy Bake Ultimate Oven for my little boy. What woman doesn't love it when a man can cook?! ;) He's almost 3, so not quite the targeted age, but we still had fun with it.

What we like:
-I like that it's purple, which is a LITTLE bit more on the neutral side.
-It cooks very quickly. You preheat for 20 minutes and then cook an average of 10 minutes or so. You get exact directions, though. I was expecting a MUCH longer cook time.

What we didn't like:
-You can't watch the food while it cooks. I wish the front was clear, and it would have made this a much better learning tool, and made it a lot more fun.
-The portions are TINY! Seriously, I don't think it would fill up a mouse! But, I guess I have to expect tiny portions for it to cook so quickly. And, I think it's more of a "time together" kind of activity!

Just some neutral information we learned. You can cook "regular" food in the oven. If you're like us, you can't pay a lot of money for tiny mixes that produce 1/10th of the size of a normal cookie. Just save a little batter from when you cook. I also learned that you CAN burn food in this oven. :) So make sure you set a timer.
The pictures in the directions have cute, perfect little cookies and cupcakes. Ours didn't even come close to looking that great. Maybe with a little more practice?!
This oven comes with a batch of cookies and cupcakes w/frosting, sugar crystals, and cupcake wraps. It also has two cooking pans and an "arm" to push the pans into the oven. It has spots marked to make sure you get them to the correct spot to cook and cool. Overall, we've had a lot of fun with it!

And this is probably obvious, but it's electric. ;)
text_fidelity_b: Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple

Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset Littlest Pet Shop Fairy Fun Roller Coaster Set is a girl's toy featuring the Littlest Pet Shop characters. It is a colorful, cute toy that offers action without the need to purchase batteries. The operation is mechanical so kids can play as long as they want without the worry of batteries dying out.

This toy is nice for many reasons and besides the lack of batteries, the toy offers some simple operation and continuous action. All your girl has to do is press the lever, which moves the stairs upward and slowly transfers the small figures and their vehicles to the top of the slide where they glide around and wind up back at the base of the stairs. If you continue to press the lever, it will gradually pick up the next Littlest Pet Shop figure and send it up the stairs to the top of the slide where it will, once again, make its way around the slide to the base of the stairs.

My girls like this toy and both they and I find it to our liking. If I had to find some type of fault, it would be the tendency for the small vehicles to sometimes get out of place when they reach the base of the stairs. I haven't witnessed any problems with the vehicles gliding smoothly down the slide- the only problem I notice is that the little vehicles will sometimes get out of place at the stairs, requiring some manual assistance to re- position them. This is most likely to happen if kids get carried away and move the lever too quickly. Keep the speed at a moderate to slow rate, and there shouldn't be any problem.

Mechanical toys are nice and even though the Fairly Fun Roller Coaster Set has little or no educational value, it is still a nice toy for girls in the target age group. It is cute, colorful, and provides hours of simple amusement without the need to purchase batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Littlest Pet Shop Fairies Fairy Fun Rollercoaster Playset

Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

text_fidelity_a:
YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls [[VIDEOID:258489d4261f7a5b0f26535ccf27c4f9]] The plusses: The game is beautiful to look at and feels good quality. The print quality is very very good, these cards do not feel cheap, they feel almost like fancy plastic. It’s also a standard size which means if you are heavy users it’s not challenging to find sleeves to accommodate. I’m also pretty sure the box is big enough to handle sleeves. The rules are relatively simple, and the instruction manual provides a QR code that leads to a video of the gameplay combined with errata to the rules as written. You will *need* the errata because the rules do not answer very basic questions. It makes me wonder how much this was play-tested with strangers before release. It’s great to see a company offering solid support after release though!

At more than 100 cards, the deck is very unwieldy to shuffle, this is definitely one that needs to be broken into smaller piles to handle and then combined.

The rounds are much shorter than expected, some rounds were over in a 2 player game in as little as three fast turns. The actual gameplay is not one “game” but to have the least points over the series of many rounds (the most “loses” the game night.) There was very little tension or any emotional investment because of the fast turnover–that might work for some folks but it didn’t feel like it was worth working on big words without stalling. There were two rounds where the game was over in two turns before my husband could even play a card. It feels like more luck than skill which is not desirable in a word game. My biggest criticism is that due to the number of repeated vowels, gameplay can feel repetitive, we started round after round with “e” or “a” despite shuffling many times. I would love to see a second deck of a different color with starting letters distributed in a more logical way because the starting letter affects the gameplay variety over time. My husband and I love wordplay and puns as a rule and this game was not skill-based enough for the two-player version for us to want to invest too much more time on it. Maybe if we played it for longer there would be more to it but we both got bored after playing 10 or so rounds and probably wouldn’t give it a second try.

The idea itself is an awesome one, when it works it’s like combining scrabble with Uno. There is solid product quality and marketing. It just lacked the skill vs luck factor for us, which may be personal taste

I really think this game needs some tweaks to the gameplay to make it better before I’d really recommend it, at least on the game shelf of a couple. It says ages 8 and up, but I can’t imagine playing this with my almost 8yo, especially without eliminating some of the rules regarding “made up words” because 50 points penalty is pretty punitive for what might be an accidental misspelling, and even with some coaching it would be pretty difficult (And my kiddo has an above-average vocabulary). Maybe several 8yo together do well? We may try to break it out at a party among adults in the future.
text_fidelity_b: YIGO - Fun & Challenging Word Game for Clever Minds - Exciting Brain Game for Kids, Teens & Adults - Improves Spelling, Vocabulary & Memory - Educational Family Card Game for Boys & Girls

Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset I usually write a review and sometimes include pros and cons, but for this item, I'm going to let the pros and cons stand almost on their own.

Pros:
- Large for the MSRP of $15 (measures 23" by 19" by 7" high)
- Simple, fun play
- Kid-powered, no batteries required
- Interesting challenge
- Unique play style for Hot Wheels with "drifting" action
- A lot of pieces in the box (12 with car)
- Can interact a little with Hot Wheels track builder track by attaching
to load a car
- Can load multiple cars (other cars not included) in line to get shot
out of the launcher one at a time
- Added play options of hitting the included flags or knocking off cars
(not included) perched at the top 3 points
- Relatively quiet play
- Perforated package back makes opening easy (this is standard to modern
Hot Wheels packaging)

Neutral thoughts:
- Not super easy to put together, but not that hard
- 6 stickers, not too many, all easy to apply
- Assembled playset segments don't sit as flush against each other,
which makes precision drifting more difficult than it should be, but
it's not that noticeable unless you're picky

Cons:
- Doesn't disassemble for storage (moreso than most of these things)
- No other way to interact with Track Builder track sections beyond loading a car, so it has to be the final part of any setup
- Parts don't have instruction's letters stamped or painted on them

It's a fun toy with few downsides, a good value and can be used with other cars. The included car is non-exclusive, but that's no big deal considering the price of the set. The action is not truly "drifting" which would be impossible with a Hot Wheels car, but it imitates drifting well via a launcher sliding the car sideways with the back facing out around the playset track. Definitely an enjoyable set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Drift Master Champion, playset

ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay is a game every age will enjoy! Kids as little as 3 love hiding and seeking and older adults love the memories of hiding and seeking out your playmates from their youth. The game can be played with 2 to 7 players.

This game is beautifully made with hard cardboard of a nice dark looking forest with a stone path. While putting the trees, stump and rock formations together, you will want to put the die under a light so it will glow in the dark for game play. You then place the masks on the Shadowling creatures. The Seeker gets to roll the die and move the lantern, after his eyes are closed, so the other player (s) can hide the little masked Shadowlings.

As the Seeker moves around the board, should any light hit any Shadowling- exposing them, their mask is removed and they are frozen and cannot move until another Shadowling can come and help him. Should all the Shadowlings end up together hiding in the same spot with their masks on, they win. Should the Seeker expose them all, freezing them, the Seeker wins. The room must be pitch black, so the tiny lantern can cast shadows and expose the hiding Shadowlings. A wonderful game of Hide & Seek played in pitch blackness that all ages will enjoy. 5 STARS.

The set up is super easy, as well as playing the game. You basically put a thick cardboard piece in place, and a couple of tubes, and you're all set. It also comes with a hexbug and 12 various colored (non-moving)bugs. Each player will get 3 of those, and the goal is to get all 3 bugs to the other side first. Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces) The Mega Construx Kadabra is better suited for display rather than actual play. His hands fall off quite easily. The play feature of the purple orb is pretty meh. But due to his ball and socket joints, he stands without needing assistance or to lean against anything.

Assembly takes about 30 minutes. The instructions are clear; the hardest part is often clicking the pieces together. My fingers actually hurt after I was finished, due to the pressure I needed to exert to get some of the pieces to fit together. I’ve noticed this with other Mega Construx sets. I wish they would fix this, as it makes it harder for young kids to do this on their own.

The set is rated 6+, which I would say is accurate for the instructions and building. The main difficulty will be snapping pieces together. I had imprints on my fingers -- that’s how hard it can be to get some pieces to fit. Which is ironic, considering how easily some other pieces, like Kadabra’s hands, fall off the finished Pokémon.

The printing on his face and chest is a lighter pink than it appears on the box.

The moustache fur is made of a floppy plastic, so it does move around when the figure is moved. This was probably my favorite part of the set, as I thought it added character to the Kadabra. A little piece of advice: I recommend fitting the moustache around the knob of the piece meant to secure it, putting it together upside down instead of the way the instructions show. This way you can ensure it’s evenly lined up.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Construx Pokemon Power Pack Kadabra Construction Set with Character Figures, Building Toys for Kids, 6 years and up (92 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
The Settlers of Catan I have lost many a Sunday afternoon to Settlers. Do you know why I purchased Settlers? Because each of my friends has purchased our own set... we do not want to find ourselves at each others house and wanting to play but not have a board to set up. We have taken turns hosting and every time it has been fun.

It is a game of strategy, in my opinion a slightly more complicated/sophisticated version of Monopoly (although my friends vehemently disagree). Instead of building houses and hotels you build towns and cities, instead of collecting rent, you collect resources, and instead of chance cards you have victory cards... but somehow it seems more fun. There is an element of Chess- because you do have to build roads to tie your cities together, and to do that you have to have foresight and plan ahead.

This is a game of champions- and voted best Table Game by folks who vote on those things- be warned that once you start playing it may become addictive. Be prepared to be suckered into the sport for years to come.

I am reviewing this product in an effort to help other Amazon customers through relaying my experience with the product and providing any insight I garnered. Had I not liked this product, I would state so here in my review. I would really appreciate that if you found my review helpful, that you would please indicate so below by clicking the YES button below.
text_fidelity_b: The Settlers of Catan

text_fidelity_a:
Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary [[VIDEOID:e1253051a67b2634f9e78ac021248ab6]] I will be the first person to admit that I purchased these because I always wanted Sea Monkeys as a kid but for some reason I never got them.

The video was shot on day 5 after I put the eggs in. There are quite a few little guys swimming around it the water and they are doing fantastic. I used spring water in their tank, kept my hands and fingers OUT of the tank and placed them in a sunny window during the day and I don't move the tank around much at all. I also aerate them for about 20 seconds every other day with a small air pump and stone that is made for fishbowls, the smallest one you can find.

Mine hatched the day after I put the eggs in.

When the kit arrived, I rinsed it out with the spring water after taking everything out of it. Then I filled it to the fill line with spring water, put the lid on it and let it sit for 24 hours.

The next day, I poured the water purifier in. I didn't stir it, I didn't mess with it at all. I poured the pack in and then put the lid back on the tank.

Next day I aerated the water then poured in the eggs. Again, no stirring or anything. I left it alone, put the lid back on and walked away.

The next day, low and behold I had teeny tiny babies swimming around.

Fed them on the 5th day after they hatched, which was a few hours before I took that video footage.

I'll update again when they are larger but so far I'm really getting a kick out of this. It would appear that the secret is less is more, spring water, don't move the tank around and a lot of patience.
text_fidelity_b: Schylling Sea Monkeys Ocean Zoo - Colors May Vary

Gege Mini : Style A Japanese Doll, Blonde, 6" (Amazon Exclusive) This Gege Mini : Style a Japanese Doll, Blonde, 6", is a remake of the Japanese 70's doll- Mademoiselle Gege, created by famous Japanese Doll Designer Midori in 1972. This new remake of Gege has the same adorable face- the typical 70's Japanese painted doll eyes, button nose, pouty small mouth with the addition of a few freckles. Her light blonde hair is styled in a typical 70's face framing style and is brushable.

Her red plastic shoes are removable as are her clothes- red pants, a lace trimmed pink polka dotted top with brown polka dotted bow and a beige canvas looking summer cap trimmed with a red ribbon and red and black fabric feathers. What makes the original Midori dolls so special are the personalities they have and happily they kept those personalities with these remakes. This adorable little Gege sucks her thumb. You may have to bend the arm with her thumb out a bit towards the doll before inserting her thumb, so it will stay in her mouth. This adorable, charming little Gege is a 5 STAR doll, just like the originals were back in 1972.

Mattel Bug Racer Vehicle the concept is pretty cool, though I still wonder if the cricket really was "deciding" where to go, or if the car just does sort of random stuff like in one of the settings. (After all, you can't see exactly what's going on in the cockpit while it's moving. The cricket is a bit too small to see clearly and know if it actually went to one side or another.)

Aside from that, the concept is really neat, especially if you have a kid that wants a pet, and you really don't want to yet or want them to start with something smaller until they learn the responsibility.

As others have noted, the car itself is great quality, and the wheels are not the junky plastic kind. They're actually rubber!

All in all, it's a little like watching the roomba vacuum robot but in a funny car shape. And that is also weirdly entertaining. Kids go NUTS for this toy, cats get scared (also funny), and it has a great setup for a starter pet or classroom toy. It has a bit of educational value, too, which is always a nice bonus, and you can combine it with a field day looking for bugs with your kids.
All in all, it's a very refreshing change from iPads and TV's. Cool toy, great quality!

text_fidelity_a:
Pass the Stache Board Game This is definitely not a cerebral or strategizing game. It is pure reaction, action, and laughter. We played a number of rounds as a way to break the ice between to families of children who had not met yet, and it was perfect. The rules are as simple as you can get, flip a card up, if it matches the color or shape of your mustache, hit it with your suction cupped mustache and claim the card. It you suction cup up one that doesn't match, you pay a two card penalty and he who ends with the most cards wins. Ok there are a couple more rules, but that is the gyst. There are also an all smash card and a none smash cards. But seriously, that is the rules right there.

The mustaches themselves are great. They are a blast in themselves as our kids giggled continually at the look of the mustaches touch to everyone's upper lip. They are made strong with decent suction cups below them. It is fairly easy to strike a card and pull it up with the suction cup. And the cards are well made to take the abuse.

As for game play, the rounds are short and exciting. Some feelings got hurt, but for the most part it was an uproarious game which put smiles on everyone's face. Scoring is easy...just count up the cards you won. Personally, I don't think this will be a classic game, but it willl be pulled out in our house many times.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

Springbok Puzzles - Eiffel Magic - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle - Large 30 Inches by 24 Inches Puzzle - Made in USA - Unique Cut Interlocking Pieces At 1000 pieces, this SPRINGBOK EIFFEL MAGIC JIGSAW PUZZLE (1000 Pieces) is definitely an “expert” puzzle. However, it goes together very quickly, because it has large blocks of unique colors--if you color-sort your pieces at the beginning, the jigsaw morphs into a series of much smaller jigsaws.

My puzzle, received in March 2019, had ALL of the pieces. No surprise, because I’ve assembled many, many Springbok jigsaws in my lifetime, and have never found one to be less than perfect. (The negative reviews suggest that Springbok temporarily had a quality control problem with this puzzle design. I sympathize with the people who received defective puzzles--even though Springbok will replace a defective puzzle, any guarantee is cold comfort when you finish a jigsaw and discover pieces missing.)

Though I wasn’t crazy about the picture, I ended up loving this jigsaw, and am saving it to put together a second time. It’s really fun to assemble, because the crazy-shaped pieces let you find fits by overall shapes as well as by design colors and patterns. There are very few dark or ambiguous pieces that are hard to place in a particular area of the design.

The only thing that I didn’t like about the puzzle is that two pieces frequently slide together side-by-side to make holes for the tabs of other pieces. This means that when you assemble a small area (e.g., the pink automobile in the middle), you can’t easily pick it up to move it to the correct location. You have to slide the assembly across your tabletop, or slide a sheet of paper under the assembly to support it as it’s moved.

Note that this is a very large (30” x 24”) jigsaw. Check to make sure that it will fit on your tabletop.
text_fidelity_b: Springbok Puzzles - Eiffel Magic - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle - Large 30 Inches by 24 Inches Puzzle - Made in USA - Unique Cut Interlocking Pieces

SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories We had so much fun with this. While we did not do the whole party element with people watching us unbox, we had a great time just on a normal day when the kids had done a great job, having a special treat of opening up each of the flaps to see what was inside.

A glow-in-the-dark boo, another boo, both with movable arms, a skeleton for around the plant and a dry bones were the highlights for us in this set. The Princess peach, also was detailed to an extent I have never seen on any of our other Princess peach figures. Usually they just fill in and under her skirt with solid plastic, and this one they gave her legs, undershorts, and high-heeled shoes underneath her dress so it is much more of a realistic figure than usual. I think either Mario or Luigi, needed a little plastic stand to be able to stand up and not just topple over. I would've appreciated a little more design on those guys so that they could be played with without an additional little clear plastic stand.

The flap opening and unveiling of the characters was a lot of fun. The characters were almost impossible in some cases to get out of the container without completely destroying the entire packaging, so my kids had to be flexible to wait until we were done opening all the flaps, then tear open the packaging to be able to push from the back and get some of those characters out. However, they were definitely firmly and securely packaged in there and were not going anywhere or getting damaged with those vacuum formed spots to sit.

Overall this was a lot of fun, and with the excellent quality of the figures, made for a very special and memorable gifting event to the kids.
text_fidelity_b: SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories
